sample_unit: older adult patients with a first normal cognitive test

links.outcome: Sociodemographic and clinical variation in EHR documentation of cognitive concerns (a source of label bias)
links.effect: 13.8% (n=2175) had a documented concern; documentation was lower with higher Area Deprivation Index, obesity (aOR 0.73) and hyperlipidemia (aOR 0.59), and higher with Parkinson disease (aOR 5.29) and commercial insurance.
links.quote: Documentation was uncommon and selectively captured by clinical and sociodemographic factors, with implications for equity and the validity of EHR-based phenotypes.

unlisted_practices: Two-stage LLM pipeline (small model screening followed by GPT-4o confirmation) for EHR phenotyping, validated against manual review

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates an LLM-based retrospective EHR phenotyping pipeline (Med42-v2-8B followed by GPT-4o) to detect subjective cognitive decline notes. It measures model accuracy and epidemiologic associations but does not evaluate an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
